revised_comments: Equatorial Guinea's digital payment market remains at an early stage of development. The country's first licensed e-money operator only began operating in mid-2023, and GETESA, the dominant telecom operator, launched its first formal mobile money and digital payments platform (GETESA Money, built on Comviva's mobiquity Pay platform) only in November 2024. Formal financial account ownership stood at around 31% of adults in 2019, and Equatorial Guinea is not covered by the Global Findex database, so no country-specific figure exists for digital payment usage. Independent 2026 ecosystem reviews describe the fintech and mobile money sector as still nascent, with fewer than ten active digital financial service providers and continuing barriers around trust, digital literacy and infrastructure. This evidence supports an estimate of fewer than 20% of adults having made an active digital payment in the past 90 days.
